name: record the heavy reasoning then recall doctrine
asks: The firm's own distribution research note (lib/emsenn/services/board-of-directors/services/executive-office/content/documents/articles/notes/2026/07/16/2026-07-16-research-on-distributing-claude-borne-work-to-scripts-and-lesser-models.md) lists as confirmed gap #1: 'Heavy-reasoning-then-recall as a compute strategy... the firm practices it... but no record states the doctrine. It is the firm's central RSI claim and deserves a first-class record.' The doctrine, stated for the record it deserves: expensive inference is spent once, to FIND a derivation; the derivation (never the bare conclusion) is stored as a checkable artifact; recall and re-check are then near-free, so capability accumulates in the ledger of checked derivations rather than in any searcher, and the searcher (any model, any tier) is replaceable without loss of accumulated capability. Transport derivations, never conclusions; price the search, not the recall.
